Medical History

  • Known hyperthyroidism.

- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded.

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health:

  • Physical activity level not discussed (patient denies weight-loss from gym).  
  • Reduced appetite; no detailed dietary assessment.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Alcohol: “once a week, couple of glasses of wine.”

Management Plan

- Arrange in-person clinic appointment for full physical examination (cardiopulmonary focus).
- Order blood tests, including thyroid function tests, at that visit.
- No medications prescribed via telehealth; treatment decisions deferred pending exam and labs.
- Clinician to brief in-clinic colleague with today’s history to avoid repetition.
- Patient advised to book appointment through clinic app.

Consider (not yet actioned):
- Comprehensive blood panel (CBC, CMP, B12, glucose, lipids) to evaluate weight loss, paresthesia, and palpitations.
- Mental health screening/support for occupational stress.
- Review of lifestyle factors (diet, exercise, sleep hygiene).
- Immunisation check and preventive health catch-up.
- CTG registration and allied health referral if indicated after assessment.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Blood pressure, pulse, BMI, waist circumference, immunisation review, comprehensive mental health screening, visual/hearing screening, urinalysis, full medication list including dose, allergy status confirmation.  
● Internal contradictions: Initial triage note listed “feeling hot”; patient clarified mainly shortness of breath—possible symptom overlap (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional incomplete sentences and brief inaudible patient responses, but key clinical details understandable.
